skill_name: Explain the difference between a TCP/IP and UDP protocol
workflow: The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and the User Datagram Protocol (UDP) are two of the main protocols used in network communications today. Both protocols provide a connection-oriented service, meaning that a connection must be established between the sender and the receiver before data can be exchanged. TCP is a reliable connection-oriented protocol, meaning that the data sent is guaranteed to arrive at the intended destination in the same order it was sent. UDP is an unreliable connection
